reasons: Section 17(b) grants the Customer (Sparkling) an unconditional right to terminate at any time on 90 days' written notice with no early-termination fee, which satisfies the rule's fallback position (Customer termination on 60–90 days' notice, no penalty).
No Vendor termination-for-convenience right exists anywhere in the termination provisions, which is better than the fallback and consistent with the preferred position on the Vendor side.

The only shortfalls versus the preferred position — 90 days rather than 30 days and the absence of an express pro-rata prepaid-fee refund on a 17(b) exit — are minor sub-elements correctly noted in the rationale rather than redlined.
Consistent with a compliant finding, no redline and no counterparty comment were proposed; the rendered redline is identical to the original paragraphs.

The failed deterministic check ('Customer convenience termination present') is a phrasing artifact: the clause says 'may terminate this Agreement at any time upon ninety (90) calendar days written notice' without using the words 'for convenience', which is substantively an unrestricted convenience right.
